title: Add RAG session-replay and end-to-end debugging guide
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: developers and SREs need a repeatable way to reproduce complex RAG sessions that involve tool-calls (search, retrieval, external APIs), model fallbacks, and KV cache behavior. Existing quickstarts show end-state examples, but debugging a flaky session (timing, injected tool errors, or cache corruption) required ad-hoc logging and local hacks. This PR introduces a session-replay specification, a playback CLI, and a short tutorial that ties together DevLoop workbench devcontainers, a vector-db stub, and example prompt/test fixtures so engineers can: 1) record a production-like session locally, 2) replay it deterministically against different model variants/quantization profiles, and 3) run assertion-driven regression tests.

What changed (high level):
- docs/rag/session-replay.md: new guide that describes the replay file format, capture hooks, best practices for recording sensitive data, and a troubleshooting checklist.
- docs/rag/examples/replay-tutorial.ipynb: hands-on notebook demonstrating capture -> replay -> assertions (with notebook outputs sanitized).
- examples/rag/replay/cli/: small python CLI (under examples) that takes a recorded session JSON and replays it with configurable model routing and injected network faults.
- examples/rag/replay/docker-compose.yml: local stack (vector db stub + redis + mock-tool server) to run e2e replay without external services.
- static/images/session-replay-sequence.svg: sequence diagram showing when to snapshot KV cache and tool outputs for deterministic replays.

Usage summary (copy-paste):
1) Start local stack: docker compose -f examples/rag/replay/docker-compose.yml up --build
2) Record a session: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=devkey; python -m examples.rag.replay.cli record --out sessions/booking_issue_2026-02-17.json --capture-kv --mask-secrets
3) Replay against a model variant: python -m examples.rag.replay.cli replay sessions/booking_issue_2026-02-17.json --model redwood/opt-2.7b-quant --inject-fault "tool:timeout,after:step:2"
4) Run tests: python -m examples.rag.replay.cli test sessions/booking_issue_2026-02-17.json --assertions docs/rag/examples/assertions.yaml

Security & privacy: the replay format supports masking rules (email/ssn/hash) and a keep-list for non-sensitive tool outputs. The docs include the recommended KMS workflow for securely storing captured sessions (avoid committing to git). See the "sensitive-data-handling" section in session-replay.md.

Limitations & future work:
- Prototype CLI is intentionally small (no production vault integration yet).
- Not all tool-call side effects are fully replayable (e.g., irreversible external API state changes). The guide recommends using mock-tool adapters for such cases.
- Replay determinism across quantized kernels depends on kernel scheduling; we document acceptable variance and regression guard thresholds.
